guideTitle: Best Mini Split Air Conditioners Under $1500 (2026)
metaDescription: Six 12,000 to 24,000 BTU mini split heat pumps at or under $1,500 from Temprium and Costway, compared on SEER2, voltage, noise claims and install needs.
expertTake: The Temprium 24,000 BTU 230V unit is the pick at this cap because 19 SEER2, a noise claim as low as 30 dB and coverage for up to 1,500 square feet make it the most capable single-zone system in the lineup. The Temprium 12,000 BTU with 22 SEER2 is the value choice for one room. Anyone sizing for a whole house should have a Manual J load calculation done instead of trusting a coverage claim.
introParagraphs: Larger single-zone mini splits are the step between a room cooler and a ducted whole-house system. They move enough heat to condition an open floor plan, a basement apartment or a garage conversion, and the inverter compressor keeps the sound level low enough to live with.

Prices move, and the $1500 cap used here reflects live listing prices when this guide was updated. At this cap the lineup runs from 12,000 to 24,000 BTU, so the guide separates what a bigger unit really buys, what the efficiency figures mean, and where an installer is not optional.

products.name: Temprium 24,000 BTU 19 SEER2 230V Mini Split AC and Heat Pump
products.description:
The Temprium 24,000 BTU is a 230 volt inverter heat pump with a 19 SEER2 rating, a claimed coverage of up to 1,500 square feet and noise as low as 30 dB. The listing stresses that an inverter modulates its output instead of cycling on and off, which is the source of its efficiency and its quiet. A two-ton class unit like this serves an open floor plan or a small house when the layout is simple.

The coverage claim is generous, since a 24,000 BTU unit typically conditions about 1,000 to 1,200 square feet in a well-insulated, open space, and rooms behind closed doors get little air from a single head. Measured against the Costway 24,000 BTU units, it states a lower noise figure and a higher SEER2 than the 18.5 model. Against the Temprium 12,000 BTU, it has twice the capacity and needs a 230 volt circuit.

A unit this size draws a heavy current, so have an electrician size the breaker and wire to the nameplate. Hire a qualified technician for the line set and refrigerant. Clean the filters monthly and keep the outdoor coil clear. In a house with a central stair or an open loft, place the indoor head where the air can fall naturally toward the living area, because a head on the wrong wall pushes cold air into a corner. If the layout includes a bedroom with a door that closes, leave that door open during the evening and let the unit equalize before bed.
products.bestFor: Open floor plans and small homes with a 230V circuit and one main living zone.
pros: Noise as low as 30 dB claimed
cons: One head cannot serve closed rooms

products.name: Temprium 12,000 BTU 22 SEER2 115V Mini Split AC and Heat Pump
products.description:
The smaller Temprium is a 12,000 BTU, 115 volt inverter heat pump with a 22 SEER2 rating, a claimed coverage of up to 750 square feet and noise as low as 23 dB. The efficiency number is the highest in the guide, and the quiet claim is the lowest, which suits a bedroom. A 115 volt supply makes the electrical job simpler than for the 230 volt units.

The 22 SEER2 and 23 dB figures are manufacturer claims measured under favorable conditions, but both point in the right direction for a bedroom or a studio. Next to the Costway 12,000 BTU with Wi-Fi, it has a higher efficiency number and a lower noise claim. Set beside the 24,000 BTU Temprium, it cools a third of the space at a much lower cost.

Coverage of 750 square feet is optimistic for 12,000 BTU, so treat 500 to 600 as realistic. Have the line set connected by a qualified technician. Clean the filters monthly and the outdoor coil each season. A quiet unit changes how you use a room, because you stop listening for the compressor and start noticing the small sounds, so the first week of ownership is when to check for rattles in the indoor wall bracket. A felt pad behind a loose bracket fixes most of them.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and studios that want the quietest and most efficient claim.
pros: Lower price tier than the big units

products.name: COSTWAY 24,000 BTU Energy Star Mini Split with 22,000 Cooling and 23,000 Heating
products.description:
The Costway Energy Star unit states a cooling capacity of 22,000 BTU and a heating capacity of 23,000 BTU from a 2 ton heat pump. It carries both Energy Star and AHRI certifications, and it works with a remote, Alexa and Google Home. The compressor speed adjusts to hold the set temperature without frequent cycling.

The stated cooling figure is lower than the 24,000 in the name, which is how honest rating works, since a two-ton nameplate often delivers a bit less. Measured against the Temprium 24,000 BTU, it carries the Energy Star label and a verified rating, but it is a heavier and more expensive unit to wire. Against the Costway 24,000 BTU with 18.5 SEER2, it adds the certification.

Certification matters if you want a utility rebate or a tax credit, so ask what the program requires. Install by a licensed technician and a permitted electrical circuit. Clean the filters monthly. Keep documentation of the model number, the serial numbers of both the indoor and outdoor units and the installer's invoice, since rebate programs often ask for all three. A smart speaker link is a nice extra, but a simple remote and a reliable thermostat matter more in daily use.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a certified efficient unit and may qualify for rebates.
pros: Works with Alexa and Google Home

products.name: COSTWAY 18,000 BTU 19 SEER2 208-230V Mini Split AC and Heater
products.description:
The Costway 18,000 BTU is a 1.5 ton heat pump with a 19 SEER2 rating, an AHRI certification and a pre-charged system. It runs on 208 to 230 volts and claims coverage of up to 1,250 square feet. Five modes, auto, cool, dry, heat and fan, and a remote cover the basics.

A mid-size unit fits the gap between a bedroom unit and a two-ton system, so it suits a large open room or a small apartment. Next to the Temprium 24,000, it costs less and draws less current, but covers less area. Set beside the 12,000 BTU units, it adds half again as much capacity and a 230 volt supply.

The 1,250 square foot claim is generous. Treat 750 to 900 as realistic for an open layout. Have a licensed electrician wire the circuit and a technician handle the refrigerant. Clean the filters monthly. The pre-charged line set is a convenience, but it is a fixed length, so measure the run from the indoor head to the outdoor pad before ordering and avoid coiling excess tubing, which hurts oil return.
products.bestFor: A large open room or a small apartment that needs more than a bedroom unit.

products.name: COSTWAY 24,000 BTU 18.5 SEER2 208-230V Mini Split AC and Heater
products.description:
The Costway 24,000 BTU without the Energy Star label has an 18.5 SEER2 rating, a 2 ton heat pump, a coverage claim of up to 1,500 square feet and an AHRI certification. It is pre-charged and runs on 208 to 230 volts with a remote and five modes. It is the plain version of the larger Costway.

Against the Energy Star Costway, it has a slightly lower efficiency and no Energy Star label, but it may cost less. Measured against the Temprium 24,000, it lists a lower SEER2 and no noise figure. As with every large unit here, the coverage claim is generous.

Size with a Manual J load calculation for anything beyond one open room. Have the circuit and line set installed by qualified trades. Clean filters monthly. The lower SEER2 number translates into a slightly higher electric bill, so ask the seller what the price difference is compared with the Energy Star model and decide whether the savings justify the premium over the life of the unit. In a mild climate that runs the unit a few months a year, the extra efficiency pays back slowly.
products.bestFor: Large open spaces where the lowest cost for 2 ton capacity matters.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A rule of thumb is about 20 BTU per square foot at an 8 foot ceiling, which puts a 24,000 BTU unit at 1,200 square feet and an 18,000 BTU unit at 900, even though listings claim 1,500 and 1,250. A single head serves only the space it can reach, so closed rooms get little air. Whole-house sizing needs a Manual J load calculation. Oversizing short cycles even an inverter. An inverter can turn down to perhaps a third of its rated output, but a unit much larger than the room still reaches the setpoint too fast and leaves the air damp. Sizing down by a notch is often the better call in a well-insulated modern room.

SEER2 is the seasonal efficiency number under the newer test, and a higher figure means lower electricity use. This lineup runs from 18.5 on the plain Costway 24,000 to 22 on the small Temprium. A unit at 22 uses roughly 15 percent less electricity than one at 18.5 for the same cooling. Compare within a size class, since larger units usually have lower numbers.

The 115 volt Temprium 12,000 BTU draws a higher current for its size but avoids a 240 volt circuit. The 208 to 230 volt units draw roughly half as much current per BTU and need the right breaker and wire. A 24,000 BTU unit often needs a dedicated 30 or 40 amp breaker. Have an electrician read the nameplate before you buy. Look for the minimum circuit ampacity and maximum overcurrent protection printed there, because those two numbers define the wire and the breaker, and an installer who sizes by guesswork can create a fire hazard. Ask whether a disconnect box within sight of the outdoor unit is required, since many codes demand one.

Energy Star and AHRI certifications verify that rated capacity and efficiency are real. The Costway Energy Star unit carries both, and the other Costway units carry AHRI. Some utility rebates and tax credits require a certified model. Check program rules before buying, since eligibility depends on the exact model. Rebates often require a matched indoor and outdoor pair listed in a directory and an installation by a licensed contractor, and the paperwork must be saved. A unit that is certified but installed outside the rules can lose the rebate, so read the conditions before you sign.

The Temprium 24,000 claims 30 dB and the 12,000 claims 23 dB, which are lab numbers at the lowest fan speed. Real noise at normal speeds is higher, and the outdoor unit adds its own sound. Place the outdoor unit away from bedroom walls. A heavy 24,000 BTU compressor is louder than a 12,000 BTU one. Outdoor noise matters to neighbors as well, so check local rules on distance to the property line and keep the pad away from a bedroom window. A rubber isolation pad under the outdoor unit cuts vibration transmitted into the ground and the wall.

Pre-charged line sets with quick connects exist for DIY work, but most places still require a licensed technician for refrigerant handling and a permit for the electrical circuit. A good installer pulls a vacuum, pressure tests the joints and documents the charge. A bad install causes noise, leaks and poor cooling. Ask what the installer will do before you commit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and sizing
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated capacities with realistic coverage. The Energy Star Costway's 22,000 cooling figure was treated as the honest number for a 24,000 BTU class unit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency and certification
howWeEvaluated.description: SEER2 values from 18.5 to 22, Energy Star and AHRI listings were weighed. Certified models scored higher for verifiability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Electrical demands
howWeEvaluated.description: Voltage and current were compared across 115V, 208 to 230V and 230V units. Heavier circuits scored lower for installation ease.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: The Temprium noise claims and the inverter operation were considered, with the caution that claims are made at the lowest speed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit at the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every item is at or under the cap on its live listing. We favored verified ratings over large coverage claims.

howToChoose.subheading: One Big Unit vs Two Small Ones

cards.label: One 24,000 BTU unit
cards.text: Lower upfront cost and one outdoor unit, but it can only serve one open zone and puts the whole load on one circuit.

cards.label: Two 12,000 BTU units
cards.text: Each room gets its own control and a smaller circuit, but two installs and two outdoor units.

howToChoose.note: Pick one big unit for an open plan and two small ones for separate rooms.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Garage or Basement Conversion Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A heat pump that works at low outdoor temperatures, a condensate drain with slope and enough capacity for poor insulation. Place the outdoor unit away from snow drifts.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Temprium 24,000 BTU and Costway 24,000 BTU units have the capacity, and the Energy Star model brings certification.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want multiple zones, a published cold-climate output table or a licensed installer's warranty. Higher tiers offer multi-zone systems and better cold-weather heat.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You condition one room, in which case a 12,000 BTU unit is enough.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter cuts airflow and efficiency. Rinse and dry.
Dust and cottonwood cut efficiency. Rinse gently with a hose.
A blocked drain leaks inside. Clear it with air.
Damaged foam causes sweating and loss. Repair or replace.
Refrigerant level and electrical connections need a technician.

faq.q: Will a 24,000 BTU mini split cool my whole house?
faq.a: Only if the house is open and well insulated. A single head serves one zone, and closed rooms get little air.
It buys single-zone 12,000 to 24,000 BTU inverter heat pumps. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.
It verifies efficiency and may qualify you for rebates. Check the program rules for the exact model.
Usually yes, for the electrical circuit and sometimes the equipment. Check local code before you start.

faq.q: How long do mini splits last?
faq.a: Twelve to twenty years with maintenance. Larger units tend to have more demanding duty.
Yes, as a heat pump. Output falls as the outdoor temperature drops, so check the low-ambient data.
